words.eg: The form {requires} two forms of identification.
words.clue: Le mot des formulaires : à l’oral on dirait « need ».

words.eg: Tickets {purchased} online are non-refundable.
You can {obtain} a copy from the office, or just ask her.
There is {sufficient} evidence to proceed, which means enough.
A {bloke} in the queue told us the whole history of the building.
I was absolutely {knackered} by the end of that week.
There is a {load of} stuff in that cupboard nobody has opened.
The wiring looked {dodgy} and the survey agreed.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces mots sont familiers. Lequel est soutenu ?
odd.why: « Sufficient » appartient au formulaire, pas au comptoir.

units.title: Remplir un formulaire, écrire un CV

words.eg: Put your {surname} in capitals, they always ask.

no.a name: Le prénom est « first name », le nom de famille « surname » ou « last name ».

words.eg: Write the {date of birth} the British way: day, month, year.
The {postcode} does half the work of the address here.
Complete the form in {block capitals} and in black ink.
You cannot be paid without a {National Insurance number}, so apply in week one.
Put the {employment history} in reverse order, most recent first.
Explain the {gap} in one line rather than hoping nobody notices.
{Tick the box} if you want to be contacted, and they will anyway.

no.to check a box: « Check » est américain ; ici on coche : « tick ».

words.eg: The first paragraph should {outline} what follows and nothing more.
One good example is enough to {illustrate} the whole point.
The {argument} is sound; the evidence for it is not.

no.a dispute: En anglais, « argument » veut dire à la fois la dispute et le raisonnement. Ici, c’est le raisonnement.

words.eg: There is no {evidence} either way, which is worth saying out loud.

no.evidences|an evidence: Indénombrable : « the evidence is », jamais « evidences ».

words.eg: To {sum up}, three of the four objections answer themselves.
The first {draft} exists to be thrown away.
{Bear in mind} that half the readers will stop at the first page.
One idea per {paragraph}, and the idea in the first line.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces mots sont des gestes d’écriture. Lequel est un état du texte ?
odd.why: Le brouillon est le texte lui-même, à un moment donné.

words.eg: Start with {Dear Sir or Madam} only when you genuinely do not know.
{Yours faithfully} goes with Dear Sir or Madam, and only with it.
words.clue: Sans le nom, c’est faithfully ; avec le nom, c’est sincerely.

words.eg: {Yours sincerely} goes with a name you have actually used.
{I am writing to} confirm the arrangements for the fifteenth.
{With reference to} your letter of the third, the answer is no.
{Please find attached} the signed copy and the revised dates.
Reply {at your earliest convenience}, which means this week.

words.en: I look forward to hearing from you
words.eg: {I look forward to hearing from you} is how nine letters out of ten end.
{Just a quick one} — are we still on for Thursday?
{Hope you’re well} is the opening line of every second email in this country.
{Sorry for the slow reply}, it has been one of those fortnights.
{Let me know} either way and I will sort the rest.
Have a look when you can, {no rush}.
Right, {speak soon} — and thanks again.
Draft attached, {any thoughts} welcome.
{Cheers for that}, it saved me a phone call.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces formules ouvrent ou ferment un message. Laquelle porte sur le délai ?
odd.why: « No rush » dit quand répondre, pas bonjour ni au revoir.

words.eg: Bring something warm, {eg} the coat you never wear.
words.clue: Du latin exempli gratia — et ce n’est pas la même chose que ie.

words.eg: The usual suspects, {ie} the three of us again.
They want it {asap}, which in this office means Thursday.
The invitation says {RSVP} by the end of the month.
The back office, {aka} the room with the kettle.
There is a {PTO} at the bottom and most people miss it.
Put {N/A} rather than leaving it blank, they send it back otherwise.
{FYI} — no action needed, just so you have seen it.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces abréviations servent à préciser un mot. Laquelle donne un délai ?
odd.why: « Asap » parle du temps ; les trois autres reformulent.
